To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose Ball Cluster Learn (BCL), a supervised approach for clustering face tracks in video.

(i) BCL is a supervised approach that can estimate the number of face clusters as well as assign face tracks to the correct cluster; (ii) BCL is able to handle face tracks of minor characters; (iii) BCL can be used as a pre-processing step to improve the clustering performance of existing methods; (iv) BCL outperforms existing clustering methods in terms of clustering accuracy and F-score, and is comparable to them in terms of clustering purity.

(a) BCL is a simple yet effective method for clustering video face tracks with an unknown number of clusters; (b) BCL is the first method to achieve state of the art results on the challenging TV series dataset; (c) BCL is able to estimate the number and assignment of clusters, and (d) BCL is easily adapted for metric learning, achieving competitive performance on a variety of datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of clustering face videos into a set of unknown number of classes.
the following question: how can we automatically cluster face tracks in videos without knowing the number of clusters a priori?
the problem of clustering face tracklets in video sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BCL outperforms the state-of-the-art in the proposed setting.
BCL is a novel and promising approach for video face clustering with unknown number of clusters, and it outperforms existing approaches on the task.
BCL is an effective approach to clustering face tracks in the presence of a large number of clusters and a large number of background characters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BCL is a simple, yet powerful, approach to face track clustering that can be applied on top of any metric learning algorithm.
we propose a new metric learning algorithm, BCL, that can be easily adapted to the task of clustering face tracks.
we propose a new metric learning method that is capable of handling the challenging problem of video face clustering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the context of clustering face tracks, the number of clusters is not an important design parameter.
the number of clusters is not a problem as long as it is estimated correctly.
the problem of video face clustering can be solved in a principled and efficient way, even in the absence of prior knowledge about the number of clusters.
